rv.q: In “Garry Starr: Classic Penguins,” the explosively silly one-penguin show, Starr avoids pants to a, shall we say, medically explicit degree.

Mr. Warren-Smith—I will call him Garry henceforth—is essentially nude throughout, and considering the wild physical activity the show entails, this constitutes a feat of chutzpah, or foolishness, that bests just about anything I have ever seen on the stage.

Happily, the delightfully zany “Garry Starr: Classic Penguins,” which has just arrived at Studio Seaview just weeks after delighting audiences at the Edinburgh Fringe, makes good on that concept to the nth degree.
This inimitable Australian comic is one of the funniest men on the planet and makes this hilarious and at times gross show a madcap and fast review of literature.
He’ll surprise you over and over again, always when you least expect it.
Garry Starr: Classic Penguins has a warm heart and a deep affection for the silliness of humanity.
I found a good deal to enjoy in the evening's inspired lunacy.

But to Mr. Warren-Smith’s credit, he channels his inner clown with such breezy wit and benevolence that you may find “Garry Starr: Classic Penguins” charming in its unapologetic, sporadically inspired silliness — that is, so long as you don’t consider full frontal nudity a deal-breaker.
Possibly not since Puppetry of the Penis has an Off Broadway show aroused such naked laughter.
Far from a classic itself, Garry Starr may not be for everyone, but at just over an hour, you can’t quite write it off.
Classic Penguins leans much too hard on immature provocation and not nearly enough on wit.
But if theater is about the power of the imagination, Garry Starr: Classic Penguins leaves nothing to the mind’s eye.
This beautiful tender city of humans needs someone as playfully joyful and talented as Damien Warren-Smith to suspend our vigilance and allow us to laugh at the glorious absurdity of everything.
The nudity eventually loses its shock value, and occasionally becomes incidental to the fun.
Your enjoyment of Garry Starr will depend on your tolerance for its audacious mode of comedy as provocation.
Those craving emotional connection beyond Starr's self-proclaimed 'lowbrow' humor will find a glimmer when he invites an audience member into an intimate hug and slow dance.

cn.t: Warren-Smith's gleefully naked clown show divides critics between those charmed by its anarchic, audience-interactive absurdity and those finding the relentless nudity and crude humor more exhausting than entertaining.

vr.q: This show is incredibly fun, and you truly never know what title or bit is going to come next.
I think with both of these ideas individually, he achieved the desired effect, and the show was extraordinarily entertaining from beginning to end.
